title: The Bakery of Maple Hollow
premise: Ines Oyelaran has spent five years keeping her heart on a strict training regimen—contained, disciplined, invisible—while her tiny café, The Bakery of Maple Hollow, slides toward foreclosure. When a freak snowstorm traps her with Theo Marchetti, the development consultant sent to buy out her block, and Amara, the estranged best friend who once broke her heart, the three are forced into a long night of confessions, flour-dusted honesty, and the best mistake of their twenties. As Ines fights to save the bakery, she discovers the buyout is a front for a corrupt land deal Theo is being pressured to execute, and that choosing the career that saved her means betraying the person who finally sees her clearly. In the end, Ines exposes the corruption at a town hearing, loses the building but wins the block's future, and chooses love—opening a rebuilt bakery with Theo while Amara, forgiven, becomes her business partner.
about_author: J. M. Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former line cook turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, small towns, and the spaces between duty and desire. They live in New England with two opinionated cats and a sourdough starter older than their marriage.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Opening on a 4 a.m. bake, we learn the bakery is three missed payments from foreclosure and Ines's creed: the heart is a muscle—trainable, containable. A letter from Marchetti Development arrives. Emotional beat: brittle control masking quiet dread.

chapters.title: The Man in the Good Coat
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo Marchetti arrives in Maple Hollow to close the block buyout, charming the town council while privately resenting his firm's pressure. He eats at Ines's café and is undone by a cardamom bun that tastes like his grandmother's. Beat: reluctant longing.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines confronts her bank, learns the buyout would erase her debt, and is tempted for the first time to surrender. Amara's name appears in old photos as she cleans the office. Beat: temptation versus loyalty to her own dream.

chapters.title: Amara
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara returns to town for her mother's surgery, carrying a decade-old betrayal: she left Ines the night of their culinary school finals to take a job abroad. She sees Ines through the bakery window and cannot go in. Beat: guilt sharpening into yearning.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The forecast turns; Ines preps for the winter festival, and Theo lingers past closing, asking questions about the block that feel too careful. A first spark of flirtation she refuses to name. Beat: warmth she doesn't trust.

chapters.title: Snowbound
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The storm hits early. Theo's rental slides into a drift; Amara's car dies outside town. Both end up stranded at the bakery with Ines, ovens running, roads closed, phones dying. Beat: forced proximity, the trap snapping shut.

chapters.title: The Best Mistake of Our Twenties
chapters.summary: Rotating POV. Over wine and emergency baking, old wounds surface: Amara's departure, Theo's complicity in the buyout, Ines's invisibility as armor. At 2 a.m., the three make a reckless pact—and Ines and Theo kiss while Amara watches, heartbroken. Beat: the mistake begins.

chapters.title: Morning After, Powder Day
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Snowbound shame and tenderness. Amara and Ines finally speak the truth of their old rupture; Theo, hungover on guilt, hides a folder of buyout documents. Beat: intimacy entangled with deception.

chapters.title: Thaw Lines
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Roads clear; Theo returns to the city office and discovers the buyout is a laundering front for a councilman's kickback scheme. His boss orders him to bury it. Beat: power's corruption made personal.

chapters.title: Counter Offer
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The firm offers Ines a generous settlement and a dream job heading a new pastry program—if she signs quietly and drops her objections. Everything she's built says yes. Beat: the career that saved everything, weaponized.

chapters.title: Flour and Ash
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara finds the buried documents Theo left in the bakery's office and recognizes the councilman's name from her own corporate past. She must decide whether to protect Ines or expose her to danger. Beat: protective secrecy breeding new lies.

chapters.title: What the Heart Is For
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines and Theo fall into a real, terrified love—mornings, shared shifts, a borrowed dog. Ines's creed cracks: the heart is a muscle, and this one is strengthening beyond her control. Beat: surrender to feeling.

chapters.title: The Councilman's Smile
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The councilman pressures Theo with threats to his career and a veiled warning about Ines's lease. Theo signs the buyout papers to buy time, lying to Ines that night. Beat: betrayal as self-preservation.

chapters.title: Signed in Ink
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara discovers the signed buyout and, believing Theo has sold Ines out, confronts him. Ines overhears the fight and learns of the documents Amara hid. Both people she loves have lied. Beat: the triangle shatters.

chapters.title: Closed for Renovations
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines accepts the firm's job offer, signs the settlement, and boxes up the bakery. She tells Theo it's over; she tells Amara they're done. The heart goes back into containment—except it won't. Beat: the false bottom of the arc.

chapters.title: The Muscle Remembers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. In the city, Theo decides to burn his career down: he copies the ledger, contacts a journalist, and prepares to testify. He chooses the person who sees him over the power that corrupted him. Beat: the moral pivot.

chapters.title: What Amara Knew
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Amara delivers the hidden documents to Ines with a full confession—she'd hidden them out of love, repeating her old sin of deciding for Ines. Ines, holding the evidence and her own signed deal, sees the trap whole. Beat: forgiveness as clarity.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. At the town council hearing, Theo testifies, the journalist publishes, and the councilman's scheme unravels. Ines tears up her settlement publicly, choosing the town and the truth over the career. Beat: climax—love against duty, duty renounced.

chapters.title: Auction Day
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The bank auctions the building anyway. The block—shopkeepers, neighbors, Amara's savings, Theo's last bonus—buys it together. The bakery is lost and won at once. Beat: belonging made tangible.

chapters.title: Rebuild
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Spring. Amara and Ines sketch a new bakery on the block they now co-own; Theo takes a job rebuilding the town's housing trust. The old betrayals are named, aired, and set down. Beat: repair without erasure.

chapters.title: First Bake
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The new ovens fire for the first time. Ines and Theo, quiet and certain, admit what the storm began; the heart is a muscle, and hers is strong now, not contained. Beat: love chosen freely, at last.

chapters.title: Open
chapters.summary: Rotating POV, closing chapter. The Bakery of Maple Hollow reopens; the town floods in; Amara hangs the sign, Theo works the register, Ines pulls the first loaves. Epilogue beat: belonging earned—visible, chosen, and home.
